guidebook.intro: In an emergency, keep it short: **Nyamba!** (help me!), **Yanguwa!** (hurry!). To say something was done to someone, Lusoga uses the passive **-ibwa / -ebwa**.

tips.title: Was stolen, is hurt
body: Add **-w-** near the end of a verb to turn it around: **okuba** (to steal) becomes **okubibwa** (to be stolen), and **okulumya** (to hurt) becomes **okulumizibwa** (to be hurt).
In the perfect, “has been …”, the ending is **-idwa**: **ebidwa** (it has been stolen), **alumizidwa** (he has been hurt).

culture.title: Getting help
body: In Uganda the emergency number for police is **999** or **112**. In a village, a loud **Nyamba!** will bring neighbours running long before any car arrives.
